gloss: to brace oneself; to prepare for the worst

definitions.gloss: to brace oneself; to steel oneself; to prepare for the worst
definitions.explanation: To mentally prepare and accept whatever outcome may come, resolving not to waver. Implies making a firm decision and facing a difficult or uncertain situation with determination.

examples.japanese: ⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧{腹|はら}を{括|くく}る⟦しかない→〜しかない：30533_shikanai⟧。
examples.english: There's nothing to do but brace ourselves.

examples.japanese: ⟦{結果|けっか}→結果：02486_kekka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦どう→どう：00543_dou⟧⟦なろう→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{腹|はら}を{括|くく}って⟦{挑|いど}む→挑む：12708_idomu⟧。
examples.english: No matter what the outcome, I'll steel myself and take on the challenge.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{腹|はら}を{括|くく}って⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{直接|ちょくせつ}→直接：03499_chokusetsu⟧⟦{辞表|じひょう}→辞表：27086_jihyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{提出|ていしゅつ}した→提出する：19644_teishutsusuru⟧。
examples.english: He steeled himself and submitted his resignation directly to the company president.

notes:
USAGE:
{腹|はら}を{括|くく}る is an idiomatic expression meaning to resolve oneself mentally for a difficult situation. The literal image is of tying up (⟦{括|くく}る→括る：04600_kukuru⟧) the belly (⟦{腹|はら}→腹：02165_hara⟧), symbolizing inner firmness. It is used when someone decides to stop hesitating and commit to a course of action, accepting whatever consequences may follow.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {腹|はら}を{括|くく}って + verb (to do something with resolve)
- {腹|はら}を{括|くく}る⟦しかない→〜しかない：30533_shikanai⟧ (there's no choice but to brace oneself)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {腹|はら}を{括|くく}る: to steel oneself (firm resolve to accept any outcome)
- ⟦{覚悟|かくご}→覚悟：02551_kakugo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{決|き}める→決める：00858_kimeru⟧: to make up one's mind (to accept a serious consequence)
- ⟦{腹|はら}→腹：02165_hara⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{据|す}える→据える：12796_sueru⟧: to gather one's resolve (very similar in meaning)
- ⟦{開|ひら}き{直|なお}る→開き直る：08204_hirakinaoru⟧: to brazen it out (giving up pretense, sometimes negatively)
